newsitem.title: FRANCE: Most French business heads see Jospin backing euro.
newsitem.headline: Most French business heads see Jospin backing euro.

text.p: A narrow majority of French business leaders thought Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's would bring France into the single European currency, according to an opinion poll made public on Wednesday.

The telephone survey of heads of businesses with at least 10 employees found that 49 percent believed he would succeed in taking France to the euro while 45 percent lacked confidence in the ability of his government to do so.
Six percent of those questioned in the Sofres poll conducted on June 10-12 had no opinion.

On a related matter, 53 percent of the business heads said Jospin should meet the January 1, 1999, deadline for European economic and monetary while 34 percent said he should impose new conditions on EMU.
Nine percent said he should abandon the single currency project altogether and four percent had no opinion.

Jospin's leftist majority, swept into power in a June 1 parliamentary election, promised during the campaign to make France's transition to the euro conditional on Spanish and Italian participation from the start and no new austerity measures.
Jospin has since deferred decisions on some key economic policy matters including state budget revisions, saying he wanted to first complete an audit of public finances, due in mid-July.
Asked whether their businesses would be ready for monetary union from 1999, 36 percent said they would be entirely prepared and 40 percent pretty much ready for the transition to the euro.
Twenty-two percent said they would not be ready in time while two percent had no opinion.
